mainEntity.name: What is the difference between air sealing and insulation, and which is more important?

acceptedAnswer.text: Air sealing and insulation are distinct but complementary components of an energy-efficient home, both crucial for reducing energy loss. Air sealing addresses uncontrolled airflow into and out of your home through cracks and gaps in the building envelope. This prevents drafts and moisture problems. Insulation, on the other hand, slows down heat transfer through conduction and convection across walls, attics, and floors. While both are vital, air sealing is often considered the first priority because it stops air movement that can bypass insulation and significantly impact comfort and energy use. A comprehensive approach involves both to achieve maximum efficiency.
acceptedAnswer.description: Air sealing stops uncontrolled air movement through gaps, while insulation slows heat transfer. Both are vital, but air sealing is often prioritized first as it directly impacts drafts and can make insulation more effective.
